lessons: A low stereo reprojection residual can coexist with a wrong surface-to-grasp-center conversion; validate the actual opposing pad contact regions.
A failed TCP verification must block gripper closure pending fresh inspection, even when the motion status says completed.
A bounded motion failure must trigger recovery even when the endpoint TCP tolerance passes; do not weaken existing tracking checks.
Hypothesis: contact-region or approach-clearance errors now limit progress more than carry speed. The current evidence does not prove this or establish that slower transport fixed prior grasp loss.
Finish occurred at actions 471, 500 and 518. Native action exhaustion alone therefore does not explain incompletion; submission availability is not shown in these excerpts.
The terminal open lid independently rules out full completion; a partial score must not be translated into a specific egg count without evaluator semantics.
Keep execution status, TCP verification, visual possession, recess occupancy and native outcome separate; completed can coexist with failed verification.
A disappearing target requires fresh visual reacquisition and cause revision, not merely converting the same estimate into an explicit position to escape freshness checks.
Stereo-band overlays constrain possible correspondence locations; they do not resolve smooth-shell identity, depth or surface-to-grasp-center conversion.
Seed 2 withdrew with the gripper open after failed descent verification; that is recovery, not evidence of grasp loss.
Finish occurred at actions 558, 552 and 583. Native action exhaustion alone does not explain incompletion; remaining submission availability is not shown.
Hypothesis: unresolved acquisition geometry remains a stronger bottleneck than carry speed. These results do not establish whether settled closure and slower carry improve retention.
